overview.description: KlÃ¡ber (also known as KalÃ¡ber, KalabriÃ¡sz, or FelsÅ‘s KalÃ¡ber) is a popular Hungarian point-trick card game closely related to Klabberjass and other games of the Jass family. It is played with a special 32-card Hungarian deck (William Tell/Seasons pattern) featuring German suits. The game is particularly popular in DoroszlÃ³ (a town in Northern Serbia with a large ethnic Hungarian population) and among Hungarian card players. It combines trick-taking with melding combinations (sequences and sets) for scoring.

history.origins: KlÃ¡ber belongs to the Jass family of games that originated in the Low Countries and spread throughout Europe. The Hungarian variant developed its own character using the traditional Hungarian deck (Magyar KÃ¡rtya) with German suits (Acorns, Leaves, Hearts, Gourds).

history.evolution: The game evolved from Klabberjass but adapted to the Hungarian card deck. The unique meld system (sequences, sets, and bella) and the anti-clockwise play direction reflect Hungarian card game traditions.
history.cultural: In DoroszlÃ³, KlÃ¡ber is played at custom-made tables with built-in slate for scoring (using chalk, not paper). The game is considered part of the cultural heritage of ethnic Hungarians in the region. Players traditionally cut the deck to settle random decisions, including who goes out for more wine.

setup.players: 4 players in fixed partnerships, teammates sitting opposite each other.
setup.deck: 32-card Hungarian deck (William Tell/Seasons pattern) with German suits: Acorns (Makk), Leaves (ZÃ¶ld), Hearts (Piros), and Gourds (TÃ¶k). Cards: Ace, King, Over Knave, Under Knave, Ten, Nine, Eight, Seven.
setup.dealing: Deal anti-clockwise in batches (not more than 3 cards at a time). Each player receives 8 cards: first 5 cards dealt, then a separate 3 cards. The last three must be kept separate from the first five until after bidding.

rules.objective: Score points by winning tricks containing valuable cards and by declaring meld combinations. The team that chooses trumps must take more than half the total card points (81+ out of 161) plus any meld points.
rules.gameplay: Play is anti-clockwise. Must follow suit if possible. If cannot follow, may play any card. Highest trump wins; if no trump, highest card of led suit wins. The last trick is worth 10 extra points.
keyRules: Player to dealer's right must bid 1 first; bidding proceeds counterclockwise.
Follow suit if possible; if void in led suit must play trump if able; otherwise any card.
Trick won by highest trump, or highest card of led suit if no trump. Winner leads next trick.
Last trick worth 10 extra card points. Contractor's team must take more than half of 161 card points plus melds.
First team to 501 points wins the game. Maccs (double game) if winners have 501+ and opponents under 251.

strategy.basic: In the bidding, remember that the player to dealer's right is forced to bid '1'. If you have strength in Acorns, you may be able to compete for the contract. Hold the Over (Jack) and Nine of trumps if possibleâ€”they are worth 34 points together.
strategy.intermediate: Meld declaration is crucial. Sequences (Terc, Kvart, etc.) and sets (Four Aces, Four Overs) can add significant points. The Bella (King and Over of trumps) is worth 40 points and nearly always scores. Plan your play to win tricks where you can claim meld points.
strategy.advanced: The Kontra round (if played) allows opponents to double the stakes if they believe the bidding team will fail. Understand when to Kontra based on your hand strength. Manage your trump cards carefullyâ€”the Over and Nine are powerful but using them at the right time is key.
tips: Always separate your first 5 cards from the last 3 during dealingâ€”you can only look at the first 5 before bidding
The Over of trumps (20 points) is the most powerful card in the deck
Four Overs is worth 200 pointsâ€”higher than most sequences
Remember the anti-clockwise direction of play and dealing
If you have the King and Over of trumps, you have the Bella (40 points)

declare.description: Declare melds: before first trick announce small melds (terc, kvart, bella); after bidding, if holding a meld worth 100+ points must declare throw-in and hand is not played.
declare.constraints: Small melds (under 100 points) announced just before playing first card to first trick. Throw-in (100+ meld) declared after trump is chosen, before play.

reveal_hand.reason: Hands are not revealed in this phase.

award_pot.reason: This game has no pot to award.

play_card.description: Play a card to the current trick. Must follow suit if possible. If cannot follow suit, must play a trump if possible. If no trump, may play any card. No obligation to beat cards already in the trick.
play_card.constraints: Follow suit if able; if void in led suit must trump if able; otherwise any card. Trick winner is highest trump in trick, or if no trump highest card of led suit. Winner leads next trick.

draw.reason: This game has no draw-from-stock action.

discard.reason: This game has no discard pile.

pass.description: Pass or yield in bidding (passz, mehet, vigyed). When two players are competing, the earlier bidder may say 'here' to equal or pass to yield.
pass.constraints: During bidding only. Once a player picks up their last three cards they must pass when their turn comes.

bid.description: Bid a number 1-4 (1=acorns, 2=leaves, 3=gourds, 4=hearts) to compete for choosing trump. Say 'here' (itt) to equal another's bid and retain right to choose trump.
bid.constraints: Player to dealer's right must bid 1 first. Others may pass or bid higher. When two bidders compete, earlier bidder has priority; continue until one passes or bid reaches 4. Final bidder names trump (must be at least the bid level).

meld.reason: Melds are declared via the declare action (announce type before first trick or throw-in if 100+); no separate meld play action.

go_out.reason: This game has no go-out action.

trumpConfig.trumpSuitRanking: Over (20), Nine (14), Ace (11), Ten (10), King (4), Under (2), Eight (0), Seven (0)

edgeCases.text: Throw-in: if any player has a meld worth 100+ points they must declare; hand is not played and meld points are compared.

Kontra: before play, opponents may double (kontra); contractor may redouble (rekontra); opponents may double again (szubkontra). Only winning team scores; points multiplied by 2, 4, or 8. No effect on throw-in.
Last trick: worth 10 extra card points to the team that wins it.
Revoke: if a player fails to follow suit or trump when able, opponents score 161 points for the hand.
Contractor wins hand: both teams score their points. Contractor loses: contractor scores 0, opponents score their points.

engine.handRankingSystem: Point-trick game; no poker hands. Card points: trump Over 20, Nine 14, Ace 11, Ten 10, King 4, Under 2, Eight/Seven 0; non-trump Ace 11, Ten 10, King 4, Over 3, Under 2, Nine/Eight/Seven 0. Last trick +10.
engine.rankingSystem: Trump order: Over, Nine, Ace, Ten, King, Under, Eight, Seven. Non-trump: Ace, Ten, King, Over, Under, Nine, Eight, Seven.
engine.deckDescription: Thirty-two-card Hungarian deck (William Tell or Seasons pattern) with German suits: Acorns (Makk), Leaves (Zöld), Hearts (Piros), Gourds (Tök). Ranks Ace, King, Over Knave, Under Knave, Ten, Nine, Eight, Seven. Same composition as a stripped 32-card deck; suits use German names and seasonal imagery on Aces.
engine.suitDescription: Four German suits used in Hungarian card games: Acorns (Makk), Leaves (Zöld), Hearts (Piros), and Gourds (Tök). William Tell deck depicts seasons on Aces and Schiller characters on the knaves; suit symbols appear in corners for identification.
engine.rankDescription: Eight ranks per suit in sequence order (high to low): Ace, King, Over Knave, Under Knave, Ten, Nine, Eight, Seven. Trick order in trumps differs: Over highest then Nine, Ace, Ten, King, Under, Eight, Seven. Non-trump: Ace, Ten, King, Over, Under, Nine, Eight, Seven.

scoring.description: Each hand: team with more card points (tricks plus last-trick bonus) and meld points wins. Game (parti): first team to reach 501 or more wins. If both pass 501 in same hand, contractor's team wins. Maccs (double game) if winners have 501+ and opponents under 251.
scoring.winCondition: Team that takes more than half of 161 card points plus meld wins the hand; first team to 501 points wins the game.
